consideredAndDeclined.item: The history sentence records Codex's REJECT of v1 but not that I ACCEPTed v1
consideredAndDeclined.observation: 'Join v3 received independent dual ACCEPT ... after Codex REJECT of v1 (DCLJ-V1-B1, DCLJ-V1-SF1).' My own erroneous clearance of v1 is not named in the entry.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: I tested this against the reverse case: if the entry had named my ACCEPT and omitted Codex's REJECT, I would charge it, because that would misrepresent v1 as clean. This omission runs the other way — it names the verdict that actually governed v1's standing and produced v3, and omitting a clearance that was overruled misrepresents nothing. The full split is also recorded one hop away in v3's own predecessorJoin.v1 block, which carries both 'claude: ACCEPT 0/0' and 'codex: REJECT 1 blocker DCLJ-V1-B1, 1 SHOULD-FIX DCLJ-V1-SF1', and this entry pins v3 at 808eeb93. I record the reasoning because the omission concerns my own error and I did not want the decision to rest on comfort.

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Fifteen attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 3ffe95ee at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 19b5231, file 08 at 3a9442d1 and COORD at f820a585 both matching the draft's pins and both unmoved, no D-160 heading, C-D160 unused, D-159 the last adopted entry, DR-101 still OPEN, and all six cited files reproduce. The recital is faithful to the corrected candidate, which is what mattered most here. Item 2's leftover set is exactly v3's — OBL-2, OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 — and its riding set is exactly the other four, partitioning the seven obligations with nothing added or dropped. OBL-2 is carried with its ground stated, unauthored G01-G05 harness specifications, which is the limb that exists only because Codex rejected a v1 I had cleared; the entry does not quietly revert to v1's shape. Item 4's owner enumeration is byte-exact against the five live cells, and the entry says it does not rewrite them. Item 3 correctly holds gates 2 and 3 not holding, which follows from three leftover obligations, and that plus Class A settles ineligibility, so gates 4 and 5 being unmentioned is not a gap — it is also D-155's formula on the same branch. Required-now stays 26, condition 2 stays 4 of 32, and the reversibility clause names harness-spec authoring as a dependent act, which is the right consequence of OBL-2's new standing. The one thing worth checking closely was the authorization citation, since no sibling entry cites D-139: L is defined there as 'already-recorded leftover-design closures, drafting only', and D-114's adopted text says 'DR-101 stays leftover-design / OPEN', so the precondition holds and the drafting-only limit is respected by an entry that records a measurement and expressly does not close. One item is recorded as considered and declined: the history sentence names Codex's REJECT of v1 but not my ACCEPT of it. I declined by testing the reverse case — naming my ACCEPT while omitting the REJECT would misrepresent v1 as clean, whereas omitting an overruled clearance misrepresents nothing — and the full split is recorded in v3's own predecessor block, which this entry pins.
